_readme: pk26/D2 — THE SHOP'S MARK, AND IT IS THIS BOX'S OWN APP THAT DRAWS IT. Same format as `seed/chrome.json`
and the same hand (`seed/blocks.mjs`): the mark simply stopped being the platform's business.
★★ WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL — THE OBJECTION IT ANSWERS: an app that places a logo in the vitrine was
changing the mark EVERYWHERE, not only where its block sits in Compose — which makes Compose meaningless,
since it configures something whose effect it cannot name. That objection was right, and it was measured:
`chrome/brand` was ONE placement read in FOUR renders — the header bar, the drawer's head, the footer's
brand column and the login modal — so an operator dragged one row and changed four places, and the board
could not say which. pk26/P1 gave each place its own slot; this file is the other half of the answer.
★★ AND IT IS THE DEMONSTRATION ITSELF, which is the second reason it is here and not in the product.
It shows a customer how they can write apps freely — the principal way Forge is extended — and it shows
it plainly and simply: one logo becoming another.
An app that lives in ONE customer's repository, writes three blocks, ships no page, asks for no
scope and changes the face of three shops is the shortest true answer to «how do I extend Forge?».
⛔ ONE COMPONENT PER PLACE — THREE, NOT ONE PLACED THREE TIMES, and this is the KERNEL'S rule rather than a
preference of ours: `placement: 'single'` is enforced per (store, app, component) by `assertSingleFree`
(packages/core/src/commands/composition.ts:176), so the same component in a second slot is refused with
`conflict`. The objection above was already the contract; it was the `chrome` app that stood
outside it.
★ THE THREE SLOTS, AND WHAT EACH DRAWS IF NOTHING IS PLACED (pk26/P1's contract):
header_brand   → storefront:header.brand          the shop's top bar                       `forge.`
drawer_brand   → storefront:header.drawer_brand   the mobile drawer's head                 `forge.`
footer_brand   → storefront:footer.brand          the footer's brand column     `forge.` + a tagline
★★ AND THERE WAS A FOURTH UNTIL pk28 — `account_brand` → `storefront:account.brand`, the login box — WHICH
LEFT THIS FILE ON THE AXIS OF THE DEPLOYABLE. The login box's mark belongs to the OOTB `chrome` app; the
demo's config keeps only the other three — the top bar, the mobile drawer and the footer — because those
three are the STOREFRONT's and the login box is the CHECKOUT's. The rule under it is trava 4 of
AGENTS.md: the VITRINE is forkable and a customer makes it theirs, so identity there may live in an app of
that customer's own — this one. The CHECKOUT is hosted by us and nobody forks it, so identity there has to
be configurable WITHOUT a fork, which makes it a capability of the product. The OOTB `chrome` app carries
the login box's mark from pk28 on; the slot itself did not move and still cedes its whole node.
⚠️ AND THE ROWS THIS FILE ALREADY WROTE DO NOT GO AWAY BY THEMSELVES — MEASURED IN THE KERNEL, 09/09.
`hook_placement` has no FK to any component registry (packages/db/migrations/tenant/0027_hook_placement.sql:8-11,
an OPAQUE reference by doctrine); nothing prunes a row whose component the manifest stopped declaring —
uninstall keeps placements (tenant/0100_composition_survives_uninstall.sql), `reconcileInstalledManifest`
and `seedDefaultPlacements` are purely additive (packages/core/src/commands/extension.ts:327-364, :526-582),
and `planBlocks` in seed/blocks.mjs only places and updates. The read keeps answering it, too: `resolveHooks`
drops a placement only when its EXTENSION is not installed and never checks the component
(packages/core/src/read/capabilities.ts:268-302). ⇒ ON A BOX THAT IS RE-SEEDED RATHER THAN REBORN the café's
old `demo-setup/account_brand` row survives, still counts as a FILL in `ExtensionOutlet` (fills are counted
BEFORE the component is resolved — packages/storefront-kit/src/extensions/ExtensionOutlet.tsx:315), and so
the slot draws NOTHING AT ALL — not even the `forge.` fallback the empty slot would give. The only hand that
removes it is `composition.remove`; a birth from zero never writes it in the first place.
★★ THE TAGLINE IS A FIELD, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE FOOTER ENTRY. «Leve. Inteligente. Sua.» is
not new: it is the Forge fallback of `footer.brand`, and that fallback cedes the node as a UNIT — mark AND
sentence together, deliberately, because «the tagline is OUR sentence: leaving it standing under somebody
else's logo would be the same defect one element to the right». So placing a mark in the footer DELETES
the sentence, and the only honest way to keep it is to SAY it. From this file on, the demo's footer says
«Leve. Inteligente. Sua.» because the demo CONFIGURED it — which is a better thing to show a customer than
a shop that inherited somebody else's line.
⛔ AND ONLY THE TWO SHOE SHOPS SAY IT — the shoe shop and the outlet, named and no others. The café has a
footer of its own and was deliberately left out; the counter has no shop window at all.
★ THE MARKS ARE THE ONES THE BOX ALREADY WORE — carried over from `seed/chrome.json`'s `brand` block,
byte for byte, so this file changes WHERE the mark is configured and never WHAT it says:
forge  → forge + .store     outlet → forge + .outlet
⚠️ BOTH ARE WORDS AND NEITHER IS A PICTURE, and that is a measurement rather than a taste. `tail` is drawn
in `var(--color-accent)`, one of the six tokens a theme redefines, so a WORD mark re-tints itself when the
theme moves (copper on the reference, carmine on the outlet) and a raster does not. The block still takes
a `logo` — it is the app's `type:'id'` field, drawn through the front's own media door — and in every
block the two are EXCLUSIVE: a picture replaces the words, and `text` becomes its accessible name.
⛔⛔ AND THE CAFÉ IS `null` SINCE pk35/d7 — THE INSTANCE REMOVED THE PLACEMENTS, UNDER THIS REPOSITORY'S
OWN RULE: a fork belongs to the customer, with 100% freedom ⇒ when a fork draws by itself what a declared block
would draw, the INSTANCE removes that store's placement (the pattern `seed/outlet.mjs:816` already uses).
⚠️ IT WAS DRESSED IN ALL THREE UNTIL THEN, AND THE SENTENCE THAT JUSTIFIED IT HAD BECOME FALSE. It read:
«the ACCOUNT screens are OURS for every store … `StorefrontChrome` … is where `header.brand` and
`footer.brand` are declared, so the café's three placements render on the screens the café's buyers reach
through us». Measured on the bench 2026-09-14, against the release `forge.lock` pins:
· the café's vitrine is the FORK. `header.brand`, `header.drawer_brand` and `footer.brand` appear
NOWHERE in `storefront-coffee/src` (0 hits), and the fork bundles its own drawing — a live fetch of
the café home renders `CoffeeChrome_*` classes and ZERO `demo-setup-*` marks;
· the ACCOUNT screens mount `StorefrontChrome` and then REPLACE both of its regions: the checkout's
layout (`apps/checkout/src/app/s/[store]/(account)/layout.tsx:70-90`) wraps header and footer in
`account.header` / `account.footer` outlets and passes the reference chrome only as a FALLBACK. The
café has `chrome/account_header` and `chrome/account_footer` placed (so does every store), so the
fallback never renders. A live fetch of the café's `/account/login` shows 0 `demo-setup-*` marks and
2 of 2 `` coming from the `chrome` app.
⇒ the three rows drew NOTHING, ANYWHERE, for the café — exactly «three rows an operator can drag and
never see the effect of», which is the sentence this same file writes for the counter.
★ AND NOTHING IS LOST BY REMOVING THEM: the café's mark on the screens WE host is carried by the `chrome`
app — `account_brand`, `account_header`, `checkout_header` all hold `forge-co-logo.png` in
`seed/chrome.json`, and they are the two images that page actually renders. The art is still this
repository's (`seed/photos/forge-co-logo.png`, the delivered cut, graded by
`bin/chrome-logo-crop.guard.mjs`); it is simply declared by the app whose blocks are the ones that draw.
⛔ AND THE COUNTER GETS NOTHING, NAMED RATHER THAN SILENTLY SKIPPED — the same rule `seed/chrome.json`
writes for the same store, and for a stronger reason here: the totem is a whole-host app of its own
(caddy `:82`, no store in the URL) that mounts neither the kit's chrome nor our account screens. Three
placements there would be three rows an operator can drag and never see the effect of.

forge._why: The reference shoe store, on the vanilla storefront image — which is what makes it the honest demonstration: no fork, no theme fork, one app placed three times and the shop is its own. The mark is TEXT (`forge` + `.store`, the tail in the theme's copper accent) and it is the same mark `seed/chrome.json` puts in the funnel's two bars as a PICTURE. ★ The footer says the sentence out loud: until pk26 it inherited «Leve. Inteligente. Sua.» from the Forge fallback, and a placed mark would have deleted it.

outlet._why: The same brand under its own theme, and the mark is where that stops being a claim: `tail` is drawn in the theme's accent — carmine here, copper on the reference — so the SAME three configs make the outlet look like the outlet without a line of code. ⚠️ THE TAIL IS `.outlet`, WITH A POINT, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING: it used to be `" Outlet"` and the header read `ForgeOutlet`, glued, because every configured word is trimmed before it is drawn and the two halves are concatenated with nothing between them. The separator has to be a printable CHARACTER. ★ The tagline is here because this is the second of the two shops named for it.
